analysis:
The complete change map shows one behavioral change: .github/workflows/release-provider.yml:239–242 explicitly selects prod for qualify-sdk tests; lines 181–182 and docs/operations/provider-release.md:315–318 explain branch-dependent defaults. The added changelog repeats that rationale. This does not itself grant production serving authorization or change the signed release lane's selected environment.
Examined workflow context at 571–1266: helper/main signing, entitlement checks, notarization, final archive verification, full CodeDirectory hashing, retained artifact identity, environment-conditioned production credentials, staging-before-publication, publication serialization and older-macOS smoke. These controls are unchanged by the supplied complete range map. Relevant contracts are A-005/A-011/A-017, T-013/T-034/T-054 and TB-010; smoke and SDK qualification must not be mistaken for independent build approval or serving permission (T-052/T-056). No changes touch prompt encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, installer execution or hold admission.
No concrete regression is established. Integration should inspect the qualify-sdk job and provider-swift/Package.swift to confirm that this override remains test-local, environment-specific build/cache separation is preserved, and production-default qualification is not represented as testing dev-specific identities. The surrounding packaged smoke checks the selected build environment at workflow:852–853, but its implementation and the affected qualification tests are outside these units. This is a coverage question, not evidence of a bypass.
